title: 🏛️ Architecture — Layers content
help: The full technical companion to 🏛️ Architecture — Layers, for the TypeScript + React build with its multi-product portfolio. For each layer and mechanism it gives the purpose, the main folders and modules, the key functions, the rules, and the data flow of one user action, then the file formats, security properties, performance budgets, the proof layer, the release procedure, the known gaps and a before / after table against the legacy single-file app.

Two things are true at once. The calculation has been ported, not redesigned: oracle fixtures recorded from the frozen legacy file prove that the engine gives the same numbers, except where a deviation is recorded on purpose (see the proof layer card). And the structure around it is new: layers enforced by tooling, a single write path, a portfolio above the single case, and a View that applies to every section.
If you are about to change code, read the layers card and the data flow card first: they tell you which layer your change belongs to and which test will catch a mistake.
body: The case is one JSON document. Screens read it through selectors and change it only through named commands; the arithmetic lives in a pure domain layer; a portfolio of products sits above the single case. This page follows the code as it is now. The version is shown in the top bar; the repository document docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is the maintained reference and the source of the known-gaps list below.

Portfolio layer: data model and consolidation flow
Since v20.0 a file is a portfolio. The decisions and phase notes are in the multi-product specification, and the user guide, both under docs/.

The rule that avoids useless tests:

maps the changed files to zones and sections and runs the test files whose import closure reaches them, plus the contract tests. Anything outside the graph (configuration, fixtures, helpers, scripts, an unknown file), the foundation zone or a very wide selection runs the full suite, which stays mandatory before a merge or a release.

Out of scope on purpose: the ADVANCED lock and its unlock gestures, and tag / MVP editing. Being ported: Gantt keyboard editing. The layout boards have a read-only in-page preview, not the legacy iframe.
Not ported: golden-versus-AME comparison, AME reference capture and per-snapshot Excel export. Agent Catalog capacity and loop external % cannot be imported, because the catalogues are immutable.
The legacy-only check TE-10b fires on two supervision fixtures in the legacy and is reproduced only in the verification section.

Multi-product, left out or not built yet: a portfolio scenarios table; dependencies and capacity between waves; shared teams across products; per-draw horizon truncation in the portfolio stress; "apply to all" for Knowledge subset fields; rates, model and coefficients per product; shared set-up at portfolio level; knowledge reuse between products; a full correlation matrix (one global rho only); item-level scope overrides (whole key only); portfolio charts as images in the results workbook.
Compatibility: a 19.x build ignores the portfolio sheets of a parameters workbook and cannot open a real portfolio file; a plain single case is still saved as v1 and stays readable.
An Excel parameters import does not re-fit the automation potential; the next file open does.
What changed since the legacy app
One global-scope script, DOM elements as the input store, HTML built from strings
Four enforced layers in TypeScript (strict) and React, files of at most 150 lines
Handlers mutate globals, then refresh everything
Every business edit is a named, undoable command; Ctrl/Cmd+Z everywhere
State registry and a JSON facade
One immutable document; the portfolio is the source of truth
Dependency graph, full refresh by default
Selectors memoised on document identity; no runtime graph
A portfolio of 1 to 50 products in waves, with a View that applies to all 86 sections
Several payback and NPV paths, three-entry sums
Time Engine owns payback and NPV; one headline owner; horizon sums for horizons 1 to 10 (see the deviations register)
Snapshot, Excel, autosave behind one manager
Same formats plus portfolio v1, portfolio workbooks, a cost model workbook and scoped reports
Oracle fixtures, deviations register, test suite, UI parity, accessibility audits, end-to-end and performance budget

Legacy engines in one line each: BUS became the command bus and audit ring; APP_STATE the store; PM the persistence adapters; DEP the derived selectors; AUDIT the verification checks and the audit log; TIME the Time Engine. The same table is on the overview page.
